$comment: Editor settings that make luau-lsp in the editor agree with luau-lsp in CI.
Without this file the extension runs on its own defaults, and the two disagree --
which shows up as type errors on files that pass the gate, or the reverse, which is
worse. The CI invocation these mirror is in .github/workflows/ci.yml, job luau-check.
If you change one, change the other.
$comment.platform: CI passes --platform=standard. The extension's default is roblox, which makes it
download and load Roblox's API dump. That is both a source of divergence and
something ADR 0020 (clean room, rule R7) has us stay away from: this engine is
written from docs/api-design.md, never from probing Roblox.
$comment.fflags: `luau-lsp analyze` enables every Luau FFlag unless told otherwise (--no-flags-enabled),
and that is what turns the new type solver on -- which rule R2 requires. Syncing flag
values from Roblox's production endpoint instead would make the editor's solver depend
on what Roblox shipped this week, so it is off.
$comment.ignore: Lute 1.0.0's own generated typedefs do not typecheck under the pinned luau-lsp 1.69.0
(M0 finding 2), so CI ignores them and so must the editor. third_party is vendored
upstream code governed by ADR 0021 and is never ours to fix.
